title: Bank Account with Static Counter
hints:
A `const` member can only be given a value in the constructor's **member initializer list**, never by assignment in the body:
```cpp
Account(std::string owner, long long cents = 0)
    : owner_(std::move(owner)), cents_(cents) { ++live_; }
```
Keep the list in the same order as the member declarations, or clang warns with `-Wreorder`.

The destructor undoes what the constructor did to the counter: `~Account() { --live_; }`, and `live()` just returns `live_`. `deposit` ignores `cents <= 0`. `withdraw` returns `false` and changes nothing unless `0 < cents <= cents_`.

`static int live_;` inside the class is only a *declaration*. Give it exactly one definition, outside the class in the same file:
```cpp
int Account::live_ = 0;
```
or, in C++17, change the declaration itself to `inline static int live_ = 0;`. Without a definition the linker fails with `undefined symbol: Account::live_`.
